paper_title: Top-K Off-Policy Correction for a REINFORCE Recommender System
authors: Minmin Chen; Alex Beutel; Paul Covington; Sagar Jain; Francois Belletti; Ed H. Chi
what_rl_controlled: Neural top-K video candidate generator, not final ranking or page composition
state: Continuous user state from historical interactions and context, represented with a recurrent model
action: Video or item recommendation from a catalog with millions of items
reward: Immediate user activity signal; live results focus on ViewTime; non-clicked recommended videos receive zero reward; long-term reward aggregated over 4-10 hours
training_data: Logged implicit feedback from previous and mixed recommender policies; exploratory traffic slice added for one experiment
training_time_period: Experiments ran multiple days; model trained continuously with new events lag under 24 hours; fixed historical calendar not reported
validation_mode: Simulations plus multiple live YouTube randomized experiments
online_or_offline_learning: Off-policy training from logged data; production experiments with continuous retraining; no real-time online policy updates
simulator_used: Simulation used to understand top-K correction; authors say realistic recommender simulation data is nonviable
deployment_scope: Production RNN candidate generator in use at YouTube; one of many candidate generators; candidates scored by a separate ranking model
baseline_or_counterfactual: Deterministic versus stochastic serving; reward-weighted control versus off-policy correction; standard off-policy versus top-K correction; K=16 production model versus K=1, K=2, K=32, and cap e3 versus e5
metrics_collected: ViewTime; videos viewed; nomination distribution by rank; reward over 4-10 hours; user activity signals
reported_successes: Exploration data increased ViewTime by 0.07 percent; standard off-policy increased videos viewed by 0.53 percent with no significant ViewTime change; top-K correction increased ViewTime by 0.85 percent and decreased videos viewed by 0.16 percent; K=8 follow-up increased ViewTime by 0.15 percent
reported_failures_or_regressions: Standard off-policy had no significant ViewTime change; K=1 lost 0.66 percent ViewTime versus K=16; K=2 was 0.35 percent worse than K=16; cap e5 lost 0.52 percent ViewTime
hard_problem_quote: simulation for generating realistic recommendation data nonviable
deployment_quote: production RNN candidate generation model in use at YouTube
why_hard_notes: Enormous nonstationary action space; sparse implicit feedback; shifting preferences; logged feedback biased by historical policies; real reward requires recommendations to real users
integration_constraints: Candidate generation only; downstream separate ranking model; outputs shown on Homepage or watch-page side panel; model is one of many generators
safety_or_guardrails: Small stochastic exploration bucket; same reward function for control and test; importance-weight capping; no unconstrained end-to-end recommender agent
evidence_notes: Primary source reports production top-K recommender at YouTube, simulations, and live experiments; effects are component tests rather than additive gains
open_questions: No dollar value reported; exact traffic scale of each live experiment not reported; no independent external audit

paper_title: Horizon: Facebook's Open Source Applied Reinforcement Learning Platform
authors: Jason Gauci; Edoardo Conti; Yitao Liang; Kittipat Virochsiri; Yuchen He; Zachary Kaden; Vivek Narayanan; Xiaohui Ye; Zhengxing Chen; Scott Fujimoto
industry_authors: All authors list Facebook; Scott Fujimoto also lists Mila, McGill
what_rl_controlled: Discrete-action DQN policy for whether to send or drop notification candidates; Horizon is the production RL platform around it
state: Person and notification-candidate features; page-administrator variant uses hundreds of features
reward: Interactions and activity on Facebook, with a penalty for sending notifications to control volume
training_data: Logged Facebook production data transformed into MDP transition records through the Spark Timeline pipeline; initial model learned from a non-RL production policy, then from traffic exposed to the RL model
training_time_period: Multiple weeks for page-administrator notifications; daily recurring updates for the push-notification model; exact calendar window not reported
validation_mode: Counterfactual policy evaluation plus a real A/B test for push-notification optimization; production deployment observations
online_or_offline_learning: Initial offline batch RL from logged off-policy production data, followed by daily retraining from model-exposed traffic
simulator_used: No production simulator reported; paper says applied settings usually lack a simulator; custom and Gym environments are used for tests
deployment_scope: Facebook production notifications for certain notification types; model package deployed through Caffe2 to thousands of machines
baseline_or_counterfactual: Prior supervised notification system based on CTR and meaningful-interaction predictions; previous production policy; CPE estimators and A/B control
metrics_collected: Activity; meaningful interactions; notification quality; CTR; daily, weekly, and monthly metrics; cumulative reward; TD-loss; MC-loss; CPE estimates
reported_successes: Real A/B test showed the RL model outperforming the non-RL control; certain notification policies significantly improved activity and meaningful interactions; page-admin model improved daily, weekly, and monthly metrics without sacrificing notification quality
reported_failures_or_regressions: No numeric regression table reported; source warns that ill-formulated RL problems can regress online metrics; fixed-batch off-policy RL can suffer extrapolation error; older page-admin supervised models traded activity against CTR
hard_problem_quote: experiments must be done with care because they don't run in a simulator
deployment_quote: significantly outperformed and replaced supervised learning systems at Facebook
why_hard_notes: Large production datasets, delayed feedback, no safe simulator, action effects on real users, and fragile MDP formulation make the problem hard
integration_constraints: Spark Timeline data join; feature normalization; action-propensity logging; ONNX export to Caffe2; PID controller keeps action distribution close to the previous production policy
safety_or_guardrails: Counterfactual policy evaluation before deployment; data-understanding checks for MDP validity; action exploration during serving; PID threshold control; unit and integration tests
evidence_notes: Primary source proves Horizon was developed and used at Facebook and reports notification RL replacing supervised systems; public numeric effect sizes are not disclosed; ABR mention is not detailed enough for a core deployment claim
open_questions: Exact effect sizes, traffic allocation, notification subtypes, and current production status are not reported; no independent audit

paper_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Optimizing Production Bidding Policies
authors: Dmytro Korenkevych; Frank Cheng; Artsiom Balakir; Alex Nikulkov; Lingnan Gao; Zhihao Cen; Zuobing Xu; Zheqing Zhu
what_rl_controlled: Parameters of an existing production auto-bidding base policy; the deployed object was not a new neural bidder
state: Campaign-level observations such as budget consumption, opportunity progress, and past bid information; full auction market state is only partially observed
action: Scalar base-policy bidding control used across auctions in a time step, then scaled by expected conversion rate inside the production auction system
reward: Aggregated value of auction outcomes won by the campaign at each time step; production metric is a proxy for aggregated impression value
training_data: Real production data from about 200,000 week-long ad campaigns, about 1.2 billion time steps, generated by the default production policy with small Gaussian exploration noise
training_time_period: Two-week production data collection on a small percentage of traffic; each production A/B test ran for one week
validation_mode: High-fidelity internal simulator for hyperparameter and checkpoint selection, followed by two large-scale online A/B tests
online_or_offline_learning: Offline RL from logged production data using modified Conservative Q-Learning; no online exploration by an under-trained learned policy
simulator_used: Yes; internal high-fidelity bidding simulator with 100 campaign configurations, one-day simulated campaigns, minute-level actions, and about 400,000 offline episodes
deployment_scope: Real Meta production auto-bidding system; optimized base-policy parameters deployed and evaluated online in large-scale A/B tests
baseline_or_counterfactual: Highly tuned production base bidding policy with default parameters; pre-test and back-test against the original base policy
metrics_collected: Main internal performance metric proxying aggregated impression value; revenue; impressions; simulation return and critic prediction diagnostics
reported_successes: Simulator CQL penalty alpha 0.1 gave stable gains above 0.5 percent after 400,000 gradient steps; production pre-test gained 0.17 percent with 95 percent CI 0.05 to 0.3 over about 50 billion impressions; production back-test gained 0.16 percent with 95 percent CI 0.03 to 0.27 over about 50 billion impressions; both tests also showed revenue gains
reported_failures_or_regressions: Exploration noise sigma_beta 0.05 caused about a 0.5 percent online performance drop during data collection, near the acceptable limit; small CQL penalty was unstable, large penalty was too restrictive; public paper reports limited production ablations because A/B slots were scarce
dollar_value_or_business_value: Exact dollar value not reported; source says slightly suboptimal policies can cause millions of dollars in losses within hours at production scale
hard_problem_quote: unsafe to deploy an under-trained agent in a production environment
deployment_quote: deployed the trained parameters of the base policy part and evaluated them online in a series of A/B tests
why_hard_notes: Thousands of auctions per second, budget constraints across campaign episodes, partial observability, advertiser funds at risk, and costly A/B tests make direct online RL unsafe and expensive
integration_constraints: Actor mean is the differentiable production base policy; neural variance and critic networks are training aids; only optimized base-policy parameters are deployed; expected-conversion-rate scaling remains part of production auction mechanics
safety_or_guardrails: Initialize from default production policy; collect data with small clipped multiplicative exploration noise; train offline with conservative Q-learning; use simulator for checkpoint choice; preserve explainable base-policy parameterization and avoid neural-network serving costs
evidence_notes: Primary source proves production data collection, offline RL training, deployment of optimized base-policy parameters, and two statistically significant production A/B tests; it does not prove a neural RL policy served bids online
open_questions: Exact product surface, traffic fraction, dollar value, and current production status are not disclosed; performance metric is internal and only described as a proxy to aggregated impression value

paper_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Sponsored Search Real-Time Bidding
venue_or_source: Proceedings of the 24th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
authors: Jun Zhao; Guang Qiu; Ziyu Guan; Wei Zhao; Xiaofei He
industry_authors: Jun Zhao and Guang Qiu; Alibaba Group
academic_authors: Ziyu Guan and Wei Zhao; Xidian University; Xiaofei He; Zhejiang University
what_rl_controlled: Hour-level parameter or model choice for sponsored-search real-time bidding, not each impression bid directly
state: Daily episode state grouped into 24 hourly steps: remaining budget, time period, and aggregated auction features such as clicks, impressions, cost, CTR, CVR, and PPC
action: Set the parameter alpha of a linear real-time bidding model for the hour; the bidding model then produces impression-level bids using predicted conversion rate
reward: Purchase amount gained in the step, with evaluation focused on purchase amount per cost under a cost constraint
training_data: Alibaba search auction logs plus simulator-generated trial-and-error data; 1000 large ads covering about 100 million auctions per day; about 200 billion simulated auctions for RL training
training_time_period: Offline log collections from two days in late December 2017; online multi-agent A/B test on February 5, 2018; one-day-ahead data collection for online training
validation_mode: Offline simulated evaluation on logged auction data plus standard online A/B tests with real advertisers and auctions
online_or_offline_learning: DQN-style learning in simulator and distributed training; trained models used online to generate real bidding decisions; no random online exploration reported
simulator_used: Yes; simulator built from complete auction logs and predicted conversion behavior to support RL exploration and trial-and-error training
deployment_scope: Alibaba e-commerce search auction platform; SS-RTB system deployed for online evaluation with real advertisers and auctions
baseline_or_counterfactual: Keyword-level bidding baseline; auction-level MDP and robust MDP offline comparisons; RMDP and M-RMDP online comparisons against keyword bidding
metrics_collected: Purchase amount per cost; conversion rate; return on investment; pay per click; cost; offline train and test performance
reported_successes: Online single-agent RMDP improved purchase amount per cost by 35.04 percent, CVR by 23.11 percent, ROI by 21.38 percent, and PPC by -5.16 percent versus keyword bidding; online multi-agent M-RMDP improved purchase amount per cost by 13.01 percent, ROI by 39.12 percent, CVR by 12.62 percent, and PPC by -0.74 percent versus keyword bidding
reported_failures_or_regressions: Auction-level MDP overfit the training day and averaged -10.06 percent on offline test data; RMDP performance dropped in the 1000-ad online setting compared with the 10-ad single-agent setting because competition among ads affected performance
dollar_value_or_business_value: Absolute values not disclosed because of Alibaba business policy; paper reports only relative improvements versus keyword bidding
hard_problem_quote: state transition probabilities vary between two days
deployment_quote: deployed the SS-RTB system in the e-commerce search auction platform of Alibaba
why_hard_notes: Sponsored search auctions have stochastic query sequences, multiple keyword bids per ad, changing cross-day transition dynamics, budget constraints, and many competing ads
integration_constraints: Control-by-model architecture: RL selects an hourly bidding-model parameter, while the real-time auction engine sends impression features to the bidding model and receives bid prices online
safety_or_guardrails: RL exploration is handled in a simulator because random bidding predictions in the online system are unaffordable; hourly aggregation reduces cross-day environment instability; multi-agent variant combines competitive and cooperative rewards
evidence_notes: Primary source reports deployment in Alibaba search auction platform, real advertisers and auctions, one-day-ahead training data for online use, and standard online A/B tests; absolute baseline values are withheld
open_questions: Traffic allocation, duration of the 10-ad online tests, durability after February 2018, absolute business values, and independent replication are not disclosed

paper_title: Reinforcement Learning to Optimize Lifetime Value in Cold-Start Recommendation
venue_or_source: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
authors: Luo Ji; Qi Qin; Bingqing Han; Hongxia Yang
industry_authors: Luo Ji; Bingqing Han; Hongxia Yang; DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group; Qi Qin work done during Alibaba internship
what_rl_controlled: Item-level lifetime-value ranking score for cold-start recommendation, combined with a conventional CTR ranking score; formal price-discount action was read-only in the live experiment
state: Item-level life-stage observations including time on market, current and accumulated PV, IPV, SLS, interested-user crowd properties, item inherent features, trend factors, and recurrent hidden state
action: Formal action contains an RL ranking score y_rl and a price-discount parameter p; in the live A/B test only y_rl took effect and p was controlled by another group
reward: ROI-like item-level reward based on next-step item page views relative to current recommendation page-view investment; cumulative LTV evaluates PV, IPV, and GMV over daily item episodes
training_data: Taobao user logs aggregated by item and day into item episodes; offline LTV recognition uses five consecutive days; live policy is warmed up from offline training and updated daily
training_time_period: Live A/B test began January 26, 2021 and lasted one week; daily item-level update frequency
validation_mode: Offline LTV recognition and ablation analysis plus live Taobao A/B test against the production Vanilla-CTR ranking baseline
online_or_offline_learning: Off-policy actor-critic with LSTM using itemwise episodic recurrent deterministic policy gradient; online ranking is real-time but RL training and updates are daily
simulator_used: No simulator reported; source emphasizes logs aggregated by item and day and live A/B constraints
deployment_scope: Taobao cold-start recommendation ranking through a dual-rank module combining the existing CTR score with the RL-LTV score
baseline_or_counterfactual: Production Vanilla-CTR ranking baseline; offline Empirical and supervised LSTM baselines; RL-LTV ablations without item inherent features, trend factors, or recurrent component
metrics_collected: PV; IPV; GMV; global PV and IPV; offline RMSE, MAE, NDCG@10, NDCG@20, NDCG@50 for LTV recognition; CTR AUC sensitivity to ranking mixture weight
reported_successes: Live cold-start items: RL-LTV improved IPV by 8.67 percent and GMV by 18.03 percent relative to Vanilla-CTR, with PV at -1.19 percent; offline RL-LTV outperformed Vanilla-CTR, Empirical, and LSTM on NDCG@10, NDCG@20, and NDCG@50 for LTV recognition
reported_failures_or_regressions: Global performance at the end of the experiment was slightly lower on PV (-0.55 percent) and IPV (-0.60 percent) versus Vanilla-CTR; RL-LTV without the recurrent component had smaller live gains; pricing action was not controlled by RL in the live experiment
dollar_value_or_business_value: GMV improved 18.03 percent for cold-start items in the live test; absolute GMV value not disclosed
hard_problem_quote: trial-and-error behavior of RL might harm the system performance, or affect the user satisfaction
deployment_quote: algorithm is deployed into production and improvements of 8 . 67% and 18 . 03% on IPV and GMV for cold-start items are observed
why_hard_notes: Cold-start items lack interaction history; mature items get exposure bias advantages; product life dynamics unfold daily while online ranking serves in real time; arbitrary live baselines are hard to launch on a platform with billions of users and items
integration_constraints: Dual-rank integration with existing CTR ranking; RL score mixed with CTR score through critic-derived weight alpha; daily item-level RL updates rather than millisecond serving-time learning; price-discount action controlled outside this RL system
safety_or_guardrails: Limited live experiment scale and depth due to customer experience and revenue risk; cold-start item groups were separated so item-based metrics could be compared fairly; mixture weight bounded between 0 and 0.2
evidence_notes: Primary source reports production deployment, Taobao live A/B test, dual-rank integration, and live constraints; it supports RL ranking investment for cold-start items but not live RL price control
open_questions: Traffic allocation, exact number of items and users in the A/B test, absolute GMV, long-run persistence, and durability after the one-week test are not disclosed

paper_title: Reinforcement Learning in the Wild: Scalable RL Dispatching Algorithm Deployed in Ridehailing Marketplace
venue_or_source: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
authors: Soheil Sadeghi Eshkevari; Xiaocheng Tang; Zhiwei Qin; Jinhan Mei; Cheng Zhang; Qianying Meng; Jia Xu
industry_authors: All authors; DiDi Labs and Didi Chuxing
what_rl_controlled: Value-informed ride-hailing order dispatch through graph edge utilities and online spatial value updates inside a maximum bipartite matching dispatcher
state: Encoded driver location or spatial grid, with tabular spatial value functions and real-time order-driver assignment information
action: Driver-order assignment recommendations selected through maximum bipartite matching; RL supplies state values, residual-value terms, smoothed rewards, completion-probability-adjusted utilities, and update rules
reward: Trip fare or driver income, smoothed by spatial rolling averages to reduce noise from dynamic pricing and incentives; performance also tracks completion rate and answer rate
training_data: Real-time trip requests and driver-order assignment streams for online TD value updates; historical data trains completion-probability classifiers; offline simulation uses DiDi real-world operational data
training_time_period: Two-week A/B testing campaign in multiple international cities; full deployment began in late December 2021 in one major international city
validation_mode: Offline simulation with real-world DiDi data, full-scale A/B testing in multiple cities, and synthetic difference-in-differences analysis after full deployment
online_or_offline_learning: Online temporal-difference value updating in pseudo-online batches; low-latency dispatch runs every 2 seconds, while value and parameter updates run every 10 seconds
simulator_used: Yes; internal simulation environment executes dispatch strategies in cities and dates using real-world daily operation data
deployment_scope: DiDi international ride-hailing markets; full-scale deployment in one major international city as primary dispatch mode, handling hundreds of thousands of daily requests
baseline_or_counterfactual: Myopic business-standard maximum matching baseline; V1D3 and CVNet-B offline comparisons; A/B time-flipping control intervals; synthetic difference-in-differences counterfactual across 37 cities
metrics_collected: Total driver income; completion rate; answer rate; anonymized primary performance metric after full deployment; low-latency calls, graph edges, and throughput measures
reported_successes: A/B weighted average improvements of 1.342 percent driver income, 0.422 percent completion rate, and 0.296 percent answer rate; full-deployment synthetic difference-in-differences analysis reports nearly 5.3 percent improvement in the primary metric; low-latency module averaged about 200 calls per second without backlog or delay
reported_failures_or_regressions: A/B effects were marginal or negative in smaller cities: City V had -0.739 percent income, -0.822 percent completion rate, and -0.867 percent answer rate; City VI had -1.102 percent completion rate and -0.300 percent answer rate; LM-UCB graph pruning was not deployed at large scale because real-time global feedback was hard to query
dollar_value_or_business_value: Driver income improved 1.342 percent on weighted average in A/B tests; absolute dollar value not disclosed
hard_problem_quote: requires both low latency and high throughput
deployment_quote: launched in one of the major international markets as the primary mode of dispatch
why_hard_notes: Supply and demand are nonstationary across space and time; dispatch needs second-level latency; cancellations occur after assignment; raw prices include dynamic pricing and incentives; region-specific constraints and sparse small-city markets affect results
integration_constraints: Existing batching and Hungarian maximum matching remain in the low-latency path; RL value updates and smoothing run in a separate high-throughput module; business constraints customize corner cases such as new drivers and long-waiting orders
safety_or_guardrails: Completion-probability adjustment; reward smoothing; graph edge standardization; adaptive learning rates; separation of low-latency dispatch from high-throughput updates; limited A/B version constrained by business rules
evidence_notes: Primary source proves online A/B tests in multiple DiDi cities and full-scale deployment since late December 2021; full-deployment performance evidence is synthetic difference-in-differences, not randomized A/B
open_questions: Exact city names, absolute income values, traffic randomization details, long-run post-publication status, and independent replication are not disclosed

system_name: Ride-Hailing Order Dispatching at DiDi via RL
paper_title: Ride-Hailing Order Dispatching at DiDi via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zhiwei Qin; Xiaocheng Tang; Yan Jiao; Fan Zhang; Zhe Xu; Hongtu Zhu; Jieping Ye
industry_authors: All authors; DiDi Labs and Didi Chuxing
what_rl_controlled: Long-term driver-location value term served inside DiDi order-dispatch combinatorial optimizer; RL changed matching edge weights rather than replacing the optimizer
state: Driver spatiotemporal state, represented by location in a hexagonal grid and time buckets; CVNet variants add contextual and transferable features
action: System assigns a driver to an order, leaves the driver idle, or allows cruising; production policy is generated by batched linear assignment over order-driver pairs
reward: Driver income from completed trips, equivalent to trip price up to a fixed share; passenger-side metrics include pickup distance, response rate, and fulfillment rate
training_data: Trip and idle-movement data for drivers, for example one month for TD(0); CVNet uses real trip training data, simulated experience augmentation, and transfer learning across cities
training_time_period: Research began in 2017; TD(0) production deployment and CVNet A/B tests are reported as of the 2021 publication; exact test calendar not disclosed
validation_mode: Historical-order replay simulation plus production A/B tests using time-slice rotation because two dispatch policies cannot run independently in the same city at the same time
online_or_offline_learning: Value functions are trained and updated offline with a Spark ETL pipeline, then served online inside the combinatorial optimizer
simulator_used: Yes; historical passenger orders replayed by day with simulated driver trajectories and behavior for policy evaluation and hyperparameter search
deployment_scope: DiDi production order dispatch; combinatorial optimizer serves all DiDi markets; TD(0) generalized policy iteration in production in more than 20 major Chinese cities; CVNet A/B tested in additional cities
baseline_or_counterfactual: Distance-based combinatorial optimization baseline using negative pickup distance edge weights; time-slice A/B rotation with three-hour intervals; simulation baselines include pickup-distance minimization and DQN variants
metrics_collected: Total driver income; order response rate; fulfillment rate; pickup distance; passenger waiting experience proxies; simulation total driver income
reported_successes: TD(0) generalized policy iteration entered production in more than 20 major Chinese cities after successful A/B tests; CVNet production A/B tests in additional cities showed 0.5 to 2 percent improvement over baseline in total driver income, order response rate, and fulfillment rate; authors translate the aggregate impact into hundreds of thousands of orders per day across China
reported_failures_or_regressions: Time-slice A/B tests can leak long-horizon benefits across alternating policy intervals; tabular TD suffers dimensionality, sparsity, and lack of cross-city transfer; DQN was less robust than CVNet in simulation; exact city-level negative results are not reported in this paper
dollar_value_or_business_value: 0.5 to 2 percent improvements in production metrics and potential equivalence of hundreds of thousands of orders per day across China; exact monetary value not disclosed
hard_problem_quote: system response time, reliability, and multiple objectives
deployment_quote: served online within the combinatorial optimizer
why_hard_notes: Huge dispatch scale, stochastic supply and demand, system latency, hundreds of cities, high QPS, changing business rules, and interference between policies in one marketplace make direct policy testing difficult
integration_constraints: Keeps batched combinatorial matching and business-rule postprocessing; learns value functions offline; serves trained values inside the optimizer; A/B testing uses time-slice rotation rather than independent user randomization
safety_or_guardrails: Production baseline favors pickup-distance edge weights to avoid long pickups and repeated neglect of short trips; rule-based eligibility and priority constraints remain postprocessing hooks; only one dispatch policy controls the city at a time during tests
evidence_notes: Primary source supports DiDi production lineage before the later KDD full-scale RLW deployment; it proves deployed RL value terms inside dispatch optimization, but does not provide the later full-scale international deployment throughput numbers
open_questions: Exact A/B dates, pilot-city list, traffic volume per test, city-level results, and current production status are not disclosed; some detailed results are deferred to cited prior DiDi papers

paper_title: A Deep Value-Network Based Approach for Multi-Driver Order Dispatching
venue_or_source: Proceedings of the 25th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
authors: Xiaocheng Tang; Zhiwei Qin; Fan Zhang; Zhaodong Wang; Yintai Ma; Zhe Xu; Hongtu Zhu; Jieping Ye
industry_authors: Xiaocheng Tang; Zhiwei Qin; Fan Zhang; Zhe Xu; Hongtu Zhu; Jieping Ye; AI Labs, DiDi Chuxing or DiDi Chuxing
academic_authors: Zhaodong Wang; Washington State University; Yintai Ma; Northwestern University
what_rl_controlled: Neural state-value estimates for multi-driver order dispatch, used to compute matching utilities inside DiDi order-driver assignment rather than replacing the matching optimizer
state: Driver location, raw timestamp, and contextual features including dynamic supply-demand features and static features such as day of week, service statistics, and holiday indicators
action: Temporally extended dispatch option moving a driver from origin to destination through a trip assignment or idle movement; production planning solves batched driver-order assignment
reward: Trip fee or total driver income over the option duration; idle movement receives zero reward; online metrics also include answer rate and finish rate
training_data: One month of driver trajectories and contextual features collected from three Chinese cities, with tens of millions of transitions and feature rows
training_time_period: One-month training data; online A/B tests reported for three Chinese cities; exact calendar dates not reported
validation_mode: Offline simulations with real DiDi data plus real-world online A/B tests on DiDi platform
online_or_offline_learning: Offline policy evaluation/value-network training from historical trajectories; trained value model used in online planning, with a distilled value function for missing real-time destination features
simulator_used: Yes; realistic simulator initialized with historical drivers and orders and periodic order-driver matching using KM/Hungarian assignment
deployment_scope: DiDi ride-dispatching platform; online A/B tests in three Chinese cities against the online production dispatching policy; support evidence for the broader DiDi dispatch system
baseline_or_counterfactual: Online production dispatching policy; simulation baselines include myopic distance-based matching, tabular value function, DQN, CVNet Basic, CVNet, and transfer-learning variants
metrics_collected: Total driver income; order answer rate; order finish rate; pickup distance in transfer simulations; robustness and value-distribution diagnostics
reported_successes: Online A/B tests report relative gains for City B of 0.60 percent answer rate, 0.49 percent finish rate, and 0.73 percent TDI; City C of 1.16 percent, 1.11 percent, and 0.93 percent; City D of 1.39 percent, 1.20 percent, and 1.65 percent; simulations report CVNet gains of 1 to 15 percent over baseline TDI and average gains of 3 to 8 percent across days
reported_failures_or_regressions: DQN underperformed in City A simulation; paper attributes this to lack of robustness treatment and the single-driver assumption; online experiment used CVNet Basic rather than full CVNet due to online system restrictions
dollar_value_or_business_value: Total driver income improved by up to 1.65 percent in reported city-level online A/B results; absolute income or dollar value not disclosed
hard_problem_quote: The production environment is intrinsically multi-agent with multiple drivers fulfilling passengers orders at the same time.
deployment_quote: We conduct real-world experiments through DiDi's platform and report online A/B testing results in Table 2.
why_hard_notes: Multi-driver marketplace coordination, temporally extended trips, nonstationary supply and demand, contextual features unavailable at destination time, and unstable neural value approximation all affect dispatch quality
integration_constraints: CVNet supplies value estimates used as utility scores in a standard matching problem; a distilled value network handles unavailable real-time dynamic destination features; production planning still solves driver-order assignment with feasibility constraints
safety_or_guardrails: Cerebellar embedding, hierarchical hexagon coarse coding, Lipschitz regularization, context randomization, and distillation are used to stabilize value estimates before they affect matching decisions
evidence_notes: Primary source reports online A/B tests on DiDi platform and describes how CVNet is embedded into the multi-driver matching planner; it is supporting evidence for the DiDi dispatch lineage rather than the chapter canonical full-scale deployment case
open_questions: Exact A/B dates, traffic allocation, city names, long-run durability, absolute business value, and whether full CVNet rather than CVNet Basic entered production are not disclosed
